newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TNT RECOMMENDS KPN TAKEOVER BID.
newsitem.headline: TNT RECOMMENDS KPN TAKEOVER BID.

text.p: Transport group TNT Ltd said on
Wednesday it had agreed to a A$2.45 per share cash takeover
offer it had received from Dutch Telecom group Koninklijke PTT
Nederland (KPN) .
The bid values TNT at A$2.0 billion. "The boards of ... KPN,
the primary postal and telecommunications corporation of the
Netherlands, and TNT Ltd, the worldwide transport and logistics
group based in Australia, announce that they have unanimously
agreed recommended cash offers made by KPN for all of the shares
of TNT," they said in a joint statement.
"The directors of TNT unanimously recommend that
shareholders in TNT accept KPN's offer, in the absence of a
superior offer, as they intend to do in respect of all of their
own shares and share options," TNT said in the statement.
The agreement followed long strategic discussions between
KPN and TNT about the benefits of combining TNT's businesses
with KPN's postal subsidiary, TNT and KPN said.
"It will create a new global force in the time sensitive
distribution and logistics industry, ranking in the top four
world-wide," they said.
TNT's share price closed up two cents at A$1.63 on Tuesday.
"This proposal represents an outstanding opportunity to
create a strong global transportation group," TNT managing
director David Mortimer said.
"For TNT shareholders, it delivers premium value," he said.
KPN chairman and chief executive Wim Dik said the
acquisition was a significant step in the company's growth
strategy.
"I am excited by the tremendous business opportunities which
will result form the combination of the excellent operations
within PTT Post, TNT and GD Express Worldwide," Dik Said.
PTT Post, a unit of KPN, said in the joint statement it
would manage the combined world-wide operations.
"This new group will allow PTT Post to broaden the scope of
its activities from mainly domestic postal operations to
world-wide time sensitive distribution and logistics," PTT Post
chief executive Ad Scheepbouwer said in the statement.
The KPN offer for TNT's preference shares includes the
A$2.45 cash plus a 6.2 cent per share dividend from TNT for the
period ending November 30, 1996.
KPN and TNT said the bid represents a multiple of 10.6 times
TNT's consolidated earnings before tax, interest, depreciation
and abnormal items and 19.1 times TNT's earnings before
interest, tax and abnormal items in the year to June 30, 1996.
It also represented a multiple of 2.6 times consolidated
fully diluted net assets per share as at June 30.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
